unit_title: An Introduction to Health and Social Care
qualification: QUALIFI Level 3 Diploma in Health and Social Care
word_count_note: Excludes index, headings, tables, images, footnotes, appendices, and reference list. Submitting significantly less may lead to refer.

formatting_rules.paragraph_form: Responses must be written in full paragraphs with appropriate headings. Bullet points and short sentences should be avoided.
formatting_rules.criterion_statement_note: Include the assessment criterion statement before each response for clarity.

referencing_requirements.minimum_citations_note: In-text citations must be included for each criterion with full references listed in the bibliography using correct Harvard formatting.
referencing_requirements.grading_impact: Absence of in-text citations or a bibliography is a refer indicator.

academic_integrity.plagiarism_policy: All submitted work must be the learner's own. Plagiarism, collusion, and self-plagiarism are academic misconduct.
academic_integrity.ai_generated_content: AI-generated content is not permitted. Submissions relying on AI-generated text lack depth and originality.

grading_guidance.pass_standard: To achieve a Pass, learners must provide clear and sufficient evidence that all learning outcomes have been met and each assessment criterion has been fully addressed.
refer_triggers: Any assessment criterion not addressed or addressed only superficially
Responses consist entirely of bullet points with no paragraph development
Irrelevant content that does not align with the criterion action verb

action_verbs.explain: Provide a clear account including why and how — not just naming something.
action_verbs.discuss: Consider the subject from different viewpoints, examining arguments for and against.
action_verbs.identify: Clearly recognise and name specific facts, features, or bodies — listing is acceptable.
action_verbs.evaluate: Judge the significance, value, or quality after studying good and bad features with evidence.
action_verbs.describe: Create a detailed picture with words — not a bullet-point list.
action_verbs.analyse: Examine carefully and in detail, identifying components and exploring relationships.

learning_outcomes.title: Understand the main roles and responsibilities of Health and Social Care workers when delivering care.

criteria.description: Explain how health and social care professionals protect individuals in their care.
criteria.guidance: Health and social care professionals are individuals who work in roles focused on supporting people's physical, mental, emotional, and social well-being across settings like hospitals, clinics, care homes, and community centres.
criteria.refer_if: The learner only names professionals without explaining how they protect individuals, or omits key concepts such as safeguarding or duty of care.

criteria.description: Discuss the mechanisms for reporting poor practice in Health and Social care.
criteria.guidance: Reporting mechanisms are the formal ways of raising concerns about poor practice, such as incident forms, whistleblowing procedures, supervision, and safeguarding referrals.
criteria.refer_if: The learner does not discuss specific mechanisms — merely stating 'you should report it' without naming formal procedures is insufficient.

learning_outcomes.title: Understand the importance of regulatory bodies in the delivery of high-quality care.

criteria.description: Discuss the roles of regulatory bodies that inspect Health and Social care provision.
criteria.guidance: Regulatory bodies are official organisations established by the government or legal framework to monitor, inspect, and regulate the quality and safety of health and social care services.
criteria.refer_if: The learner only names the CQC without discussing what it does, or does not discuss any inspection role or regulatory function.

criteria.description: Identify the professional bodies that regulate the professions within health and social care.
criteria.guidance: Professional bodies regulate individual practitioners, ensuring fitness to practise and professional standards — distinct from regulatory bodies that inspect services.
criteria.refer_if: The learner confuses regulatory bodies (CQC) with professional bodies (NMC, GMC), or only names one professional body without identifying others.

learning_outcomes.title: Evaluate the role of the interprofessional team in delivering Health and Social care.

criteria.description: Explain the roles and responsibilities of the inter-professional team in meeting care needs in the case study.
criteria.guidance: An inter-professional team is a group of professionals from different disciplines (e.g., doctors, nurses, social workers, therapists) who work together to plan and deliver coordinated, person-centred care. The response must reference the case study provided in the assignment brief.
criteria.refer_if: The learner provides a generic description of team roles without referencing the case study, or does not explain how different professionals collaborate to meet the individual's needs.

criteria.description: Discuss the difference between multi-disciplinary and inter-professional team working.
criteria.guidance: A multidisciplinary team consists of different professionals working on the same case but may not fully share decision-making or collaborate as closely as inter-professional teams.
criteria.refer_if: The learner treats MDT and inter-professional working as identical, or simply defines one without discussing the differences between them.

criteria.description: Discuss the potential barriers to teamwork and how they could be overcome.
criteria.guidance: Barriers to teamwork include factors such as poor communication, different priorities, unclear roles, or lack of shared information.
criteria.refer_if: The learner only lists barriers without discussing how they could be overcome, or provides only one barrier with no depth.
